items.title: Jack Lesberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997
items.q: during the 40s alone you were with Louis Armstrong and Teagarden and Coleman Hawkins and Sidney Bechet and Sarah Vaughan.

ctx.x: Well I didn’t stay at Condon’s very long after that. I got quite busy with studios and I wound up, oh I did the original Milton Berle Show when it went color, with color T.V. That started a whole new era there. And I was on The Bell Telephone Hour, and The Hit Parade with Raymond Scott for a number of years I did. I freelanced. I found I preferred freelancing. I missed a couple of good things that I wanted to do, and when you were on staff there you could only work a certain number of days, it had certain…

Well I was looking at this little discography and so forth, and during the 40s alone you were with Louis Armstrong and Teagarden and Coleman Hawkins and Sidney Bechet and Sarah Vaughan. Either you couldn’t hold a job or people liked you.

Sarah, I played her audition. And Leonard Feather had her up there and they had George Auld. We didn’t get any money for it. And she was about 15 years old. She was a scrawny little gal. And I got to know her very well later in years. She came to Australia when I lived there and I toured with her for George Wein later on. And so it was a wonderful relationship knowing people of different parts of the jazz music and the scene. People like Ruby Braff, and some unusual musicians.
